sections.overview: Ciliocincta julini is a microscopic marine orthonectid parasite recorded from the spionid polychaete Scolelepis fuliginosa on the French Atlantic coast.
sections.identification: The free reproductive stages have a ciliated, ringed body, but reliable field identification is difficult because the animals are minute and live within a host.
sections.habitat: Its known host record comes from a marine polychaete at Anse Saint-Martin, Cap de la Hague; the available record does not establish a broad range.
sections.diet: As an internal parasite, it uses host tissues rather than hunting independent prey; species-specific nutritional details remain undescribed.
sections.behavior: The ciliated sexual stages leave the host, a life-history pattern reported for orthonectids as a group; the timing and behavior of C. julini are poorly known.
sections.reproduction: The 1992 redescription places this species in Ciliocincta and identifies its polychaete host, while the reproductive cycle is known mainly from broader orthonectid studies.
sections.ecology: Its ecological existence depends on a particular marine worm host; it can be compared directly with C. sabellariae, described from a different polychaete host.
sections.conservation: No species-level population trend or conservation assessment was found; the single historical locality and host record leave its status uncertain.
